stops.note: to sing, giving rise to cantus (song), combined with dis- (apart)
a singing apart, a melody sung against a main tune, from dis- and cantus
stops.meaning: a melody sung against a main tune

stops.note: carried into French for a musical counterpoint melody
settled as the English word for a melodic line sung above the main tune
stops.meaning: a melodic line sung or played above the main tune

current_meaning: a melodic line sung or played above the main melody, or to talk at length on a subject
